label: Bible Study
prompt: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more _____.
verse: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
note: The thief takes; the Good Shepherd gives life — and more of it.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath _____ a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
verse: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
note: What God starts, He finishes — Paul writes this confidence in chains.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Jesus increased in wisdom and _____, and in favour with God and man.
verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
note: Luke's summary of Jesus' quiet years in Nazareth: growth in wisdom, stature, and favour with God and man.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of _____, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
verse: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
note: Fresh off the Hall of Faith in chapter 11, the stands are full — so drop the extra weight and run.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had _____ of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.
verse: And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.
note: The men of Issachar 'had understanding of the times' — every leadership sermon's favorite tribe.
